title: Small-office network with VLANs, inter-VLAN routing and DHCP
summary: Design, build and document a small-office network in Cisco Packet Tracer with VLANs, trunks, router-on-a-stick routing, DHCP and a written addressing plan.
why: It shows you can turn requirements into a working, documented network, which is the core of help desk, network technician and junior network engineer roles. A clean diagram, an addressing plan and saved configs are exactly what a hiring manager hopes to see.
brief:
A small company has four groups on one floor: Staff (about 50 users), Sales (about 25), Guest Wi-Fi (up to 100 devices) and Management (network devices only). Build their network in Cisco Packet Tracer (or Cisco Modeling Labs): two access switches joined by a trunk, one router doing inter-VLAN routing with subinterfaces (router-on-a-stick), and the router acting as the DHCP server for every user VLAN.

Start with an addressing plan. Subnet one private block (for example 10.10.0.0/22) with VLSM so each VLAN has room to grow, reserve the first addresses of each subnet for the gateway and static devices, and record it all in a table. Use a separate management VLAN for the switch SVIs and a native VLAN that carries no user traffic. Move unused ports into an unused VLAN and shut them down.

Constraints: each trunk allows only the VLANs it needs; each DHCP pool excludes gateway and static addresses; every device has a hostname, every uplink has a description, and every configuration is saved. Finish with a test plan that proves hosts get the right addresses and can reach the other VLANs, plus a short troubleshooting log of what went wrong while you built it. (Keeping guests away from internal VLANs is the job of ACLs, which the secured edge project adds.)

milestones.title: Addressing plan and diagram
tasks: List each VLAN with its ID, name, host count and purpose
Subnet 10.10.0.0/22 with VLSM, largest subnet first
Draw the topology with interfaces, VLANs and trunk links labeled
milestones.doneWhen: A table lists every VLAN's subnet, mask, gateway, DHCP range and broadcast address, and no two subnets overlap.

milestones.title: VLANs and access ports
tasks: Create and name the VLANs on both switches
Assign access ports with switchport mode access and switchport access vlan
Put unused ports in an unused VLAN and shut them down
milestones.doneWhen: `show vlan brief` on each switch matches the plan exactly.

milestones.title: Trunks
tasks: Configure the switch-to-switch link and the router uplink as 802.1Q trunks
Set the same dedicated native VLAN on both ends and limit the allowed VLANs
Turn off DTP negotiation with switchport nonegotiate
milestones.doneWhen: `show interfaces trunk` on both switches shows the same native VLAN and only the planned VLANs allowed and forwarding.

milestones.title: Router-on-a-stick
tasks: Create one subinterface per VLAN with encapsulation dot1Q and the gateway address
Bring up the physical interface with no shutdown
Verify with show ip interface brief and show ip route
milestones.doneWhen: A Staff host can ping its gateway and a Sales host, and the router shows a connected route for every VLAN subnet.

milestones.title: DHCP
tasks: Exclude gateway and static ranges with ip dhcp excluded-address
Create a pool per user VLAN with network, default-router and dns-server
Set the hosts to DHCP and check show ip dhcp binding
milestones.doneWhen: Every user host receives an address, mask, gateway and DNS server from the correct pool.

milestones.title: Test plan and write-up
tasks: Run a test matrix: each VLAN pings its gateway and every other VLAN
Write up two problems you hit, the show commands that revealed them and the fixes
Export each device's running configuration to a text file and save the .pkt file
milestones.doneWhen: The repository contains the test matrix with results, the troubleshooting log, one config file per device and the .pkt file.

stretch: Replace router-on-a-stick with a Layer 3 switch using SVIs, and compare the two designs
Add a wireless access point for the guest VLAN
Give the switches a management SVI reachable only by SSH (a preview of the secured edge project)
rubric: A reviewer should see a VLSM addressing plan with non-overlapping subnets sized for each VLAN
A reviewer should see a labeled topology diagram that matches the actual build
A reviewer should see trunks with a non-default native VLAN, a limited allowed list and DTP turned off
A reviewer should see unused ports shut down and moved out of VLAN 1
A reviewer should see DHCP pools that exclude gateway and static addresses
A reviewer should see a test matrix with results and a troubleshooting log
A reviewer should see running configurations exported as text, not only a .pkt file
showcase: Create a GitHub repository with folders for configs (one text file per device), diagrams and docs, and put the topology diagram and addressing table at the top of the README
Include the Packet Tracer .pkt file so reviewers can open the lab themselves
Write the troubleshooting log as symptom, show command used, cause and fix; employers value this more than the configs
List it under Projects on your resume with the repository link, and share a screenshot of the topology on LinkedIn
resumeBullet: Designed and built a 4-VLAN small-office network in Cisco Packet Tracer with VLSM addressing, 802.1Q trunking, router-on-a-stick inter-VLAN routing and DHCP; documented the addressing plan, configs and test results on GitHub.
interviewTalkingPoints: How you sized each subnet, and why you allocated the largest first
Why you changed the native VLAN and shut down unused ports
How a frame from a Staff host reaches a Sales host: tagging, the router subinterface and back
A problem you troubleshot and the show commands that found it
